text:
Great work. The Intel GPUs are so hard to test due to their CPU overhead issue. The way this was tested really helps understand the implications, although even this is close to the ideal scenario for the card. One, it's at 1440p, so we're staying as close as possible to a GPU bound scenario, and two, the Ryzen 5 5600 is still a relatively new (still being made and sold) and relatively fast CPU, so while the testing certainly shows the overhead issue that the card has, it's still not the slaughter that we can have at 1080p (which is what probably most of these cards are going to be doing), especially with older AM4 AMD or pre-12th gen Intel CPUs.

All things considered, I can't but think that Intel has dropped the ball this time (or again) and the Arc B cards came to us only to become another part of the narrative of how compromised the entry level GPU segment is (with the prices of $200-$250 being considered 'compromised entry level territory' certainly not being the least of the compromises).
